headline: Grid Dark: 340,000 Shelf Residents Lose Power in Suspected Infrastructure Failure
body:
A catastrophic failure in Substation 7-Gamma has left 340,000 residents of The Shelf without power as of 2300 hours last night — and Ironclad, the substation's operating contractor, is giving no timeline for restoration. The failure cascaded through three secondary relay nodes in under four minutes, suggesting either catastrophic equipment degradation or deliberate interference, though Ironclad representatives have refused to speculate publicly. Emergency lighting in only 40% of residential corridors is functional, running on local battery reserves that medical workers warn will begin failing within 48 hours in the sector's two understaffed clinics. 'My mother is on a NovaMind-assisted cardiac monitor,' says Efrain Guerrero-Yip, a resident of Level 14, Block F. 'I have been told to bring her somewhere with power. Where exactly is that supposed to be?'

Meridian Metro Authority activated a Level 2 Emergency Designation at 0100 hours, authorizing the deployment of six mobile generation units to critical care facilities. As of this broadcast, three of those units have not arrived. The Shelf's 19-story residential stacks — built by Palladian under 2098 federal housing codes — have no gravity-independent water circulation, meaning upper-floor residents now have no running water in addition to no power. Temperature in the northern Shelf sectors is currently 3 degrees Celsius and falling. The Collective has opened four emergency warming stations in community halls, running off locally-maintained off-grid solar reserves.

The blackout entered its sixth day before any official Ironclad crew was sighted in the district. A leaked internal memo, published by Lake Monitor, indicates Ironclad flagged Substation 7-Gamma for critical maintenance in 2118 and was denied budget approval by the Meridian Infrastructure Authority twice. The blackout would ultimately last twenty-two days — the longest in The Shelf's history. Six confirmed deaths have been attributed to the outage, a number community advocates say is 'deliberately minimized.'
aftermath: A Lake Monitor investigation published in early 2121 confirmed that Ironclad executives approved the maintenance budget denial to protect a dividend payout, resulting in a class-action suit that was quietly settled for 18 million quanta with no admission of liability.
runner_relevance: The 22-day blackout generated a sprawling runner economy of necessity. Medical supply smuggling contracts from The Circuit to The Shelf's clinics ran at 1,200 to 2,800 quanta per load as legitimate supply chains stalled. Wealthy Shelf residents hired protection runners to guard generator fuel stockpiles from desperate neighbors, spawning ethically murky but well-paying guard contracts at 800 quanta per night. The Collective hired couriers to coordinate between its warming stations in conditions where BCI comms were degraded by power fluctuation. Graycloaks paid data-retrieval rates of 7,500 quanta for anyone who could extract Ironclad's internal maintenance records — the memo that eventually broke in Lake Monitor was runner-sourced. Post-blackout, infrastructure sabotage investigation contracts from Ironclad targeted suspected activist groups.
